name: Korea: From the Three Kingdoms to K-pop
description: Two thousand years of a peninsula between giants: kingdoms and an alphabet, invasions and occupation, a divided land, and a southern republic that took its culture to the world.

checkpoints.name: The Three Kingdoms
checkpoints.note: Goguryeo rules the north and into Manchuria, Baekje the south-west from near today's Seoul, and Silla the south-east. Tomb paintings show early hanbok dress. With Chinese help Silla defeats Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668 and rules most of the peninsula.

checkpoints.name: Goryeo
checkpoints.note: Goryeo, the kingdom that gives Korea its name in English, absorbs Silla in 935. Kimchi appears on its tables. When the Mongol Empire invades in the 1200s, monks carve the Tripitaka Koreana on more than eighty thousand wooden blocks as a prayer for the country's survival.

checkpoints.name: The Joseon kingdom
checkpoints.note: The Joseon dynasty makes Seoul its capital and builds the Gyeongbokgung palace in 1395. Its fourth king, Sejong the Great, has scholars create Hangul, an alphabet simple enough for ordinary people to learn. Records also mention the armoured turtle ship for the first time.

checkpoints.name: Invasions from all sides
checkpoints.note: Toyotomi Hideyoshi sends Japanese armies into Korea in the Imjin War. Admiral Yi Sun-sin's fleet and troops of the Ming dynasty drive them out by 1598. Three centuries later Korea is the prize in the First Sino-Japanese War and the Russo-Japanese War, and Japan wins both.

checkpoints.name: Occupation and division
checkpoints.note: The Empire of Japan annexes Korea in 1910, and the March First Movement of 1919 demands independence. Samsung starts as a trading firm in 1938. In 1945 the country is split, North Korea under Kim Il Sung and South Korea form in 1948, and the Korean War ends with the DMZ in 1953.

checkpoints.name: The South rises
checkpoints.note: Park Chung Hee seizes power in 1961 and drives fast industrial growth under harsh rule. The Gwangju Uprising of 1980 is crushed, but democracy wins out, the 1988 Olympics come to Seoul and Kim Dae-jung becomes president. K-pop, Gangnam Style, BTS and Bong Joon-ho's Parasite win audiences around the world.
